comment: Conformance for the pack: what a solution asks, placed on a machine that grants it (PLC-1). Every case is a machine file and the packs placed on it, carried inside the case; the machine is host.machine in the court. An accept names the services and users the placed machine must declare, in order. A reject names WHERE its refusal must land -- the file and the line, in that file's own numbering -- and the fragment it must contain, so refusing for the wrong reason or at the wrong place fails. The pin is declarative/pack/PINNING.md.

accepts.name: a pack with an identity, a budget and a health window, placed on a machine that grants what it asks
accepts.machine:
DEFINE MACHINE core AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "The machine a solution is placed on"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "A solution serves on the network"
DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "Its data lives on a declared mount"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS tmpfs, OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "Where the solution keeps what it keeps"
DEFINE SERVICE front AS (
  RUN ["/front"],
  RESTART always,
  READY "/run/front.ready",
  NEEDS [network]
) RATIONALE "The machine's own door"

packs.source:
-- commons.pack -- the Commons, asked for.
DEFINE USER commons_user AS (
  UID 2001
) RATIONALE "The Commons runs as itself and owns nothing of the machine"

DEFINE SERVICE commons AS (
  RUN ["/stzr", "/app/commons.luau"],
  RESTART always,
  READY "/run/commons.ready",
  HEALTH 5,
  AFTER [front],
  NEEDS [network, filesystem],
  SEES [data],
  USER commons_user,
  MEMORY 256,
  CPU 100,
  TASKS 64
) RATIONALE "Catalogue, orders and payments; it serves once the machine's door is up"
